inputs.sbc_source: No stock-based compensation add-back on the FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement (4901.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:1027-1047); the only equity-award line is 'Stock acquisition rights' in the statement of equity (lines 979, 1005), movements of -697m / +223m JPY, immaterial against 3.36tn revenue. Treated as an SBC-zero filer: SBC rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: 30.0bn JPY buyback resolved 2026-03-30, executed April 2026 (Q1 FY2027 financing: 'Sales (purchase) of stock for treasury' -30,002m, 4901.T_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:686), 9.73m shares cancelled. FY2026 itself repurchased only 12m JPY. Count is held flat; with zero SBC there is no grant dilution to offset, so buybacks are optional capital return, not a modelling convention.
inputs.share_count_basis: Issued 1,234,150,284 less treasury 38,542,505 at 2026-06-30 = 1,195.6m basic (4901.T_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:86-87), plus ~1.0m dilutive stock acquisition rights implied by FY2026 basic/diluted EPS 229.65/229.45 (4901.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:1363-1368) = 1,196.6m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is zero, so there is nothing to dilute; buybacks are not projected.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Short-term debt 307,269 + long-term debt 668,333 = 975,602 total interest-bearing debt (bonds, borrowings, CP) less cash and cash equivalents 150,651 at 2026-06-30 (4901.T_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:440,497,511). Operating lease liabilities (37,944 current + 96,817 non-current) are EXCLUDED because the lease cost is already inside operating income under ASC 842; no finance leases disclosed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. Risk-free: 10y JGB ~1.7% (Oct 2026). Japan ERP 6.0%, beta 1.0 for a large-cap diversified industrial/healthcare conglomerate -> cost of equity ~7.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt 0.6% (FY2026 interest expense 4,993m on ~790bn average interest-bearing debt), ~0.45% after tax. Weights at market: equity 4.19tn (81%), debt 0.98tn (19%) -> WACC 6.3%, rounded to 6.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality (semiconductor materials, Instax discretionary), CDMO ramp execution and the print-segment decline are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost is already expensed inside operating income, so it is inside the EBITDA margin path (treatment B equivalent). Operating lease liabilities (134.8bn JPY at 2026-06-30) are therefore excluded from net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path is charged separately -- charging it would double-count.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; noncontrolling interests (5,065m JPY at 2026-06-30, 0.1% of equity) are deducted once in the equity bridge. FY2026 NCI share of net income was 562m, immaterial.
inputs.non_operating_assets: Interest and dividend income (11,222m FY2026) and equity-method earnings (1,929m) sit outside operating income and are NOT in the projected flows, so their source assets are added in the bridge at book: investment securities 43,672m and investments in affiliated companies 37,617m (2026-03-31, 4901.T_Annual_FY2026.txt:674-677). Cash is already in net debt.
inputs.capex_cycle_note: PPE+software capex ran 3.4-6.6% of revenue in FY2016-FY2022 (D&A ~5%), then 11.3% / 15.7% / 17.5% / 17.0% in FY2023-FY2026 as the Bio CDMO build-out (North Carolina, UK, Denmark, Toyama) peaked. Management's FY2027 (year to March 2027) forecast is 338bn tangible + 66bn software = 404bn (11.3% of guided revenue), down 178bn YoY, with FCF guided to turn positive and Healthcare capex stated to have peaked (4901.T_Presentation_FY2026.txt:742-760, 1298-1308; reaffirmed in Q1 FY2027 presentation lines 1010-1025). D&A is guided to 210bn (5.9%) and will keep rising as 980bn of construction-in-progress enters service. The model therefore does NOT use the latest-year or average recent FCF as a base; it builds each year from components with capex gliding from the guided 11.3% toward a 7.0% mature level (base) against D&A maturing at ~6.5%. That glide is the mid-cycle normalisation.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (routing row: operating company, non-US and cyclical; owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md read). Fujifilm is a diversified operating conglomerate (Healthcare 33%, Business Innovation 35%, Imaging 19%, Electronics 14% of FY2026 revenue), not a bank/REIT/holdco, so the FCF engine applies. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). FY0 is FY2026 (year ended 31 March 2026, US GAAP, JPY). Horizon 10 years because the owner-FCF margin is still ramping (capex normalising, Bio CDMO margin recovering) and is not mature by year 5. Terminal cap multiple 15x FCF (below the 20x default) for a cyclical conglomerate with a structurally declining print segment. Quote and reporting currency are both JPY; no FX bridge. Price is a regular TSE close, not after-hours. The August 2026 Business Innovation partial spin-off is a potential value-unlock catalyst (bull axis) but is 2-3 years out and subject to approvals, so it is not modelled as a separate scenario.

equity_bridge.item: Investment securities (cross-shareholdings, at balance sheet value)
Investments in and advances to affiliated companies

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 company revenue guidance (3,560bn vs 3,357bn FY2026, +6.0%, raised Aug 2026) -- used as year-1 growth, then decelerated toward terminal
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.7% exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR 8.9% by 32% and EPS 8.8% by 33%. The equity series is inflated by yen-weakness translation gains in accumulated OCI (+303bn JPY in FY2026 alone, 736bn cumulative) and by retained earnings accumulating during a period when FCF was negative; it is not a cash-return signal. Base growth is anchored to guidance and revenue history, not to the equity CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF (OCF - PPE - software) because SBC is zero and net cash is absent. Owner FCF was 295bn (FY2021), 158bn (FY2022), -113bn (FY2023), -57bn (FY2024), -130bn (FY2025), -160bn (FY2026): the FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative end point) and are set to null. The collapse is entirely capex (126bn FY2022 -> 571bn FY2026) while OCF held at 324-428bn and EPS compounded 8-9%/yr. 5yr window FY2021-FY2026 (FY2021 was the COVID trough, so the 8.9% revenue CAGR flatters); 3yr window FY2023-FY2026. EPS is diluted, split-adjusted (3-for-1, April 2024).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = FY2027 guidance +6.0%. Then decelerates 0.5pp/yr: Healthcare (CDMO fill, endoscopy, IVD) and Electronics (AI semiconductor materials) high-single-digit, Imaging (Instax) mid-single-digit, Business Innovation (35% of revenue) flat-to-declining. Blended 3yr history is 5.5%.
base.margin_rationale: FY2027 guided EBITDA = OI 365bn + D&A 210bn = 575bn = 16.2% of 3,560bn (FY2026 actual 15.6%). Ramp to 18.5% by year 7 as Healthcare OI recovers from the guided 41bn trough toward 120bn+ when North Carolina phase 1 and Toyama fill (each 1% of group revenue in CDMO margin is ~0.4pp), partly offset by Business Innovation decline and silver/memory input costs. 18.5% EBITDA (~12% OI) sits below the VISION2030 ambition of 10%+ ROE by company-FY2030, which implies roughly 14% OI / 20% EBITDA.
base.da_rationale: Guided 210bn FY2027 (5.9%); rises toward 6.5-6.6% as 980bn construction in progress is commissioned, then settles as capex normalises.
base.capex_rationale: Year 1 = guided 404bn / 3,560bn = 11.3%. Glides to 7.0% by year 6: above the 6.5% D&A run-rate to fund mid-single-digit growth, and above the 3.4-6.6% pre-cycle range because the CDMO and semiconductor-materials businesses are more capital-intensive than the print business they are displacing.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 current tax 80.7bn / EBIT 350.2bn = 23.0%; FY2025 24.8%; total effective 24.9%. Ramps to 27% as US/Japan profits grow (Japan statutory ~30.6%, blended lower by overseas mix).
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer with receivables 763bn + inventories 601bn vs trade payables 390bn: growth consumes cash. FY2026 operating asset/liability changes were -49bn on +161bn revenue (-30%), FY2025 roughly neutral; -10% capture of the revenue change is the through-cycle assumption, with CCC improvement (116 -> 106 days) as the offset.

bull.narrative: CDMO fills on schedule and the semiconductor-materials upcycle persists; margins reach the VISION2030 ambition (~20.5% EBITDA, 10%+ ROE); capex falls faster to 6.5%.

bear.narrative: CDMO utilisation keeps slipping, the second North Carolina phase and Toyama keep capex at 8-11% of revenue, Business Innovation shrinks, input costs (silver, memory, oil) and a stronger yen compress margins to 15%; D&A on under-utilised plant rises to 7%.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue grows 6% in FY2027 per the raised guidance, decelerating to 2% by year 9. The Bio CDMO ramp recovers over three to four years rather than one: Healthcare operating income climbs back from the guided 41bn trough as North Carolina phase 1 (eight 20,000L bioreactors, operating since March 2026), the UK drug-substance building and Toyama (FY2027 start) fill with contracted volume from Janssen, Regeneron and new clients; Electronics rides AI-driven photoresist/CMP/advanced-packaging demand; Instax keeps growing mid-single digits; Business Innovation drifts down and is partially spun off within 2-3 years without changing group economics in the model. Group EBITDA margin rises from 16.2% to 18.5% by year 7. Capex falls from the guided 404bn (11.3%) to 7% of revenue by year 6, so owner FCF turns positive in year 1 and reaches roughly 7% of revenue at maturity. Terminal value is capped at 15x year-10 FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Both secular bets land together: the CDMO facilities reach high utilisation on schedule with new large-scale antibody contracts, and the AI semiconductor-materials cycle extends (Rapidus, India capacity, advanced packaging). Margins reach the VISION2030 ambition (~20.5% EBITDA, 10%+ ROE) and growth stays at 6-7% for four years. The Business Innovation spin-off crystallises a cleaner Healthcare/Electronics multiple. Capex normalises faster, to 6.5% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: CDMO execution disappoints again: utilisation ramps slip, regulatory inspections idle small/medium facilities, and the second North Carolina phase plus Toyama keep capex at 8-11% of revenue for years while Healthcare operating income stays near the FY2027 trough. Business Innovation's print decline accelerates, the semiconductor cycle turns, and silver, memory and Middle East-driven energy costs (management's own 30-40bn/quarter oil risk) plus a stronger yen compress EBITDA margin to 15%. Growth fades to 1%. FCF stays barely positive through the horizon.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the thesis rests on a capex ramp that has already slipped once (Healthcare FY2027 OI guidance cut from 69bn to 41bn within three months, segment loss in Q1 FY2027) and because the largest segment by revenue is in secular decline. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs two independent things to go right (CDMO fill AND a sustained semiconductor-materials upcycle) plus a spin-off that is 2-3 years out and subject to approvals.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fujifilm is valued as a going-concern operating conglomerate on owner FCF built from components, not on its recent reported FCF, which is distorted by a capex supercycle (571bn JPY in FY2026 against a 125-166bn pre-cycle run-rate). The judgment is in the capex glide (guided 404bn in FY2027, normalising to ~7% of revenue), the recovery of Healthcare margins as new CDMO plants fill, and a 15x terminal cap that refuses to pay a growth multiple for a business whose largest segment is shrinking. Discounted at a JPY WACC of 6.5%; risk is in the scenario flows and the 25/50/25 weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex does not normalise: a second North Carolina phase, Toyama and semiconductor-materials capacity keep capex above 10% of revenue beyond FY2027 (each 1pp of capex is ~35bn JPY/yr of FCF, ~30 JPY/share of PV per year it persists)
CDMO utilisation and margin recovery slower than the three-to-four-year base ramp; Healthcare operating income stuck near 41bn instead of recovering to 120bn+
Business Innovation (35% of revenue) decline accelerates or restructuring costs recur; the spin-off removes a cash-generative segment
Input costs (silver assumption doubled to 400,000 JPY/kg, memory -25bn JPY OI headwind, oil at $100 = 30-40bn JPY/quarter) and a stronger yen against the 150 JPY/USD guidance basis
Discount-rate sensitivity: a terminal-heavy valuation at a 6.5% JPY WACC; each +1pp WACC removes roughly 12-15% of value
Terminal cap at 15x FCF binds in the base and bull scenarios; a market paying a higher multiple for a 'pure' Healthcare/Electronics Fujifilm post spin-off is upside not in the house number
